_comment: Some book queries deliberately show bare :name / :n parameters with no \set — the book uses them to illustrate passing values from application code (regresql-style bind params, see queries/regresql/plans/), not psql variables. Running one of these directly in query-ui would hit an unresolved ':name' and fail. Each entry here is the literal \set line(s) query-ui prepends when serving that file, so it's immediately runnable — the .sql files on disk are untouched. Values are illustrative sample data, not part of the book's text. QUOTING: a plain \set name 'Queen' stores the *unquoted* text Queen (psql strips the assignment's quotes the same way a shell would) -- fine for a query that itself does :'name' (the query adds the quotes back at substitution time), but wrong for a query using bare :name where a string is expected, which needs the *stored value itself* to already contain literal quote characters: \set name '''Queen''' (the doubled '' decode to one literal quote, same trick the book uses for \set season 'date ''1978-01-01'''). Check which form (:name vs :'name') the target query actually uses before adding an entry.
